title: Adobe Premiere Pro Advanced Core v2

domain.name: Adobe Premiere Pro Advanced
domain.description: Advanced Premiere production covering longform architecture, multicam, conform, audio, color management, After Effects integration, transcription/caption operations, mastering, and delivery QC. Version-specific UI details belong in Current Intelligence.

competencies.name: Longform Project Architecture
competencies.description: Structure large projects, productions, sequences, shared media, review paths, and archive states for long-running editorial work.
competencies.purpose: Keep complex edits stable across weeks, collaborators, and revisions.

units.title: Editorial structure is an information system
units.content: Bins, productions, sequence versions, review exports, shared assets, cache, and archive locations should make current state and provenance obvious.

units.title: Longform setup workflow
units.content: Define source-media authority, naming and sequence version rules, shared-asset boundaries, review/export paths, autosave/backup locations, and archive policy before edit complexity grows.

units.title: Longform failure modes
units.content: Avoid editing from ambiguous duplicate sequences, storing originals among exports, uncontrolled relinks across drives, and deleting old versions before the approved master is confirmed.

drills.title: Architect a documentary-style project
drills.prompt: Design Premiere organization for many shoot days, interviews, b-roll, music, revisions, and social derivatives.

competencies.name: Advanced Multicam, Sync & Drift Control
competencies.description: Handle long recordings, mixed timecode, external audio, variable drift, and source replacement safely.
competencies.purpose: Keep event and performance edits synchronized over long runtimes.

units.title: Sync can be correct at one point and wrong later
units.content: Independent clocks and variable frame/audio behavior can cause drift even when initial sync is perfect.

units.title: Longform multicam workflow
units.content: Choose a master timing reference, verify sync at beginning/middle/end, label angle and audio ownership, correct drift before heavy editing, preserve original sources, and test source replacement on representative sections.

units.title: Multicam failure modes
units.content: Avoid syncing only one clap point on long sessions, switching master audio unintentionally, flattening too early, and fixing drift by random micro-cuts across an edited sequence.

drills.title: Stabilize a long event multicam
drills.prompt: Plan sync and drift correction for three cameras plus board and recorder audio across several hours.

competencies.name: Proxy, Conform & Media Management
competencies.description: Manage offline/online workflows, relinking, proxies, mezzanine media, metadata, and final conform.
competencies.purpose: Edit efficiently without losing the path back to authoritative camera originals.

units.title: Editorial media and finishing media can differ
units.content: Proxy or mezzanine workflows are safe only when stable identifiers, timecode, filenames, reel/camera metadata, and source provenance allow deterministic reconnection.

units.title: Conform workflow
units.content: Validate source metadata, generate or attach proxies, edit without renaming originals casually, lock approved sequence, relink to originals, spot-check effects and speed changes, then verify final media paths before master export.

units.title: Conform failure modes
units.content: Avoid approximate filename relinks, transcoding away needed metadata, mixed frame-rate assumptions, and deleting proxy or original relationships before the master is verified.

drills.title: Conform an offline edit to camera originals
drills.prompt: Create a safe relink and verification plan for a project edited from proxies across multiple drives.

competencies.name: Advanced Dialogue & Mix Workflow
competencies.description: Control dialogue cleanup, clip gain, buses, music, ambience, automation, loudness, and export handoff.
competencies.purpose: Produce clearer mixes and cleaner downstream audio workflows.

units.title: Gain structure comes before processing
units.content: Processors behave more predictably when source levels are sensible before compression, limiting, noise reduction, and bus processing.

units.title: Advanced editorial mix
units.content: Organize dialogue/music/effects roles, normalize source gain, repair only what needs repair, route shared processing logically, automate musical and scene changes, monitor loudness/peaks, and export stems when handoff requires them.

units.title: Mix failure modes
units.content: Avoid aggressive denoise that damages speech, solving every level issue with a limiter, masking dialogue with music, and delivering without checking actual exported audio channels.

drills.title: Mix a live-event highlight
drills.prompt: Plan dialogue, room tone, music, crowd, effects, bus processing, automation, and QC for an event film.

competencies.name: Color-Managed Premiere Workflow
competencies.description: Handle mixed camera gamuts, log media, transforms, scopes, adjustment layers, and export color behavior coherently.
competencies.purpose: Reduce color surprises between source, timeline, monitoring, and delivery.

units.title: Source interpretation, working space, look, and display transform are separate
units.content: Color problems become easier to diagnose when technical transforms are separated from shot correction and creative look decisions.

units.title: Managed-color workflow
units.content: Identify source spaces, verify interpretation, choose timeline/output intent, normalize technically, balance and match shots, apply creative look deliberately, review scopes and monitor path, then test actual export playback.

units.title: Color-management failures
units.content: Avoid stacking LUTs without knowing their role, double transforms, judging log footage from viewer appearance alone, and assuming one platform interprets exported tags like another.

drills.title: Normalize a mixed-camera project
drills.prompt: Design the color pipeline for log, standard, and phone footage in one sequence.

competencies.name: Dynamic Link, MOGRT & Motion Integration
competencies.description: Coordinate Premiere and After Effects templates, linked comps, renders, versioning, and handoff without brittle dependencies.
competencies.purpose: Use motion graphics at scale while preserving editorial responsiveness.

units.title: Cross-application links create dependency chains
units.content: Dynamic Link and templates can accelerate iteration but also create version, cache, font, plugin, and path dependencies that must be tracked.

units.title: Motion-integration workflow
units.content: Define which graphics stay templated versus bespoke, lock naming and source paths, expose only intended MOGRT controls, render intermediate masters when dependency risk grows, and test handoff on a clean system or user profile.

units.title: Integration failure modes
units.content: Avoid dozens of heavy live-linked comps late in delivery, undocumented fonts/plugins, editing source comps from unknown versions, and rendering final outputs without dependency checks.

drills.title: Design a scalable Premiere/After Effects graphics pipeline
drills.prompt: Plan recurring lower thirds, score graphics, transitions, and custom hero shots for a series.

competencies.name: Transcription, Captions & Text-Based Operations
competencies.description: Use transcripts, captions, search, text-driven edits, and accessibility workflows while validating automated output.
competencies.purpose: Accelerate editorial navigation and delivery without trusting automation blindly.

units.title: Automated transcription is assistive evidence, not ground truth
units.content: Names, slang, music, accents, crosstalk, and noisy recordings can produce errors that must be reviewed before captions or editorial decisions become final.

units.title: Transcript-to-caption workflow
units.content: Generate or import transcript, verify names and high-impact phrases, use text search/editing as a navigation aid, create caption structure, review timing/readability, and export in the format required by the current delivery platform.

units.title: Caption workflow failures
units.content: Avoid publishing raw automated transcripts, letting captions cover key graphics, trusting punctuation and speaker labels automatically, and freezing platform-specific caption rules into permanent doctrine.

drills.title: QC an automated caption pass
drills.prompt: Create a review process for a music/interview video with slang, names, background music, and rapid speech.

competencies.name: Advanced Mastering & Delivery QC
competencies.description: Create archival masters, review exports, platform derivatives, captions, metadata, and repeatable QC evidence.
competencies.purpose: Make delivery trustworthy and reproducible across clients and platforms.

units.title: QC validates the exported artifact, not the timeline
units.content: The deliverable can differ from the sequence because of encoder, color, audio, caption, frame-rate, metadata, or media-reference problems.

units.title: Mastering workflow
units.content: Lock the approved sequence, create a high-quality master, verify duration/frame rate/resolution/color/audio/captions, watch critical sections and transitions, inspect file metadata, then derive platform versions from the verified master where appropriate.

units.title: Delivery failure modes
units.content: Avoid exporting derivatives from different sequence versions, relying on old presets for current platform specs, skipping first/last-frame checks, and archiving without project/source provenance.

drills.title: Build a delivery QC matrix
drills.prompt: Define QC for master, YouTube, vertical social, client review, and captioned versions of one project.
